scope: order_items table — composition_snapshot column type + immutability invariants + 6 INSERT/copy-forward sites. READ-ONLY.

findings.title: composition_snapshot column is plain JSON nullable — no DB-level immutability guard

evidence.down_migration: Same file:21 — `$table->dropColumn('composition_snapshot');` (no trigger to drop = no trigger was created)
evidence.fillable: OrderItem.php:31-56 fillable array contains 'composition_snapshot' on line 44 → mass-assignment allowed

findings.comparison_with_NF525_protected_tables: audit_logs and z_reports tables have BEFORE DELETE triggers (`SIGNAL SQLSTATE '45000'`) per CLAUDE.md §8. order_items.composition_snapshot has NO equivalent BEFORE UPDATE trigger to enforce NF525 §V immutability.
findings.actual_state: Immutability enforced by call-graph convention only — see Security F5-SEC-03.
findings.v1_1_recommendation: Add migration creating MySQL trigger `BEFORE UPDATE ON order_items FOR EACH ROW IF OLD.composition_snapshot IS NOT NULL AND NEW.composition_snapshot <> OLD.composition_snapshot THEN SIGNAL SQLSTATE '45000' SET MESSAGE_TEXT = 'order_items.composition_snapshot is NF525-immutable'; END IF;`. SQLite test envs can use a generated-column constraint or skip the trigger entirely with the model-level mutator guard.

findings.title: Six composition_snapshot write sites reconciled — 5 INSERT (builder-driven) + 1 COPY-FORWARD (refund)

copy_forward_site.operation: OrderItem::create([...'composition_snapshot' => $item->composition_snapshot, ...]) creates a -qty mirror row with snapshot bytes IDENTICAL to parent → NF525 §V invariant preserved (chain reads same composition for refund)

findings.consequence: Reconciliation matches the Z-5 attest (5 builder-driven INSERT + 1 refund copy-forward). The 4 legacy INSERT sites are dead code today (pinned-off flag) but still pass NF525 invariants because they delegate snapshot construction to the same CompositionSnapshotBuilder.
findings.v1_1_recommendation: Post-C.5, only PricingService.php:291 + RefundWithCounterEntryService.php:136 remain as snapshot write sites. Add a unit test asserting `grep 'composition_snapshot' app/` returns ≤2 write contexts (sentinel against drift).

findings.title: OrderItem cast 'composition_snapshot' => 'array' silently auto-decodes — masks json_encode/decode discipline

explicit_encodes: PricingService.php:291, OrderService.php:466/821/1277, FrontendOrderService.php:441 — all `'composition_snapshot' => json_encode($compositionSnapshot)` for OrderItem::insert() (raw mass-insert bypasses Eloquent cast)

findings.consequence: Eloquent's 'array' cast applies to model instances (`OrderItem::create()` + `->save()` paths) but NOT to mass-insert (`OrderItem::insert([...rows])`). Hence the 5 INSERT sites all wrap the snapshot in `json_encode()` manually. The 1 COPY-FORWARD site at RefundWithCounterEntryService.php:136 uses `OrderItem::create([...])` → Eloquent cast applies → it passes `$item->composition_snapshot` which is ALREADY the decoded array (read via cast). End result is correct (cast re-encodes on save), but the asymmetry is fragile: a future maintainer might switch the 5 INSERT sites to `OrderItem::create()` and forget to remove `json_encode()` → double-encoded snapshot (invisible until NF525 reprint).
findings.v1_1_recommendation: Document this convention in CompositionSnapshotBuilder docblock + add a unit test asserting all snapshot writes produce a single-level JSON (parse `composition_snapshot`, assert `is_array($decoded) && !is_string($decoded)`).

findings.title: OrderItem soft-delete + BranchScope global scope are CONSISTENT with NF525 retention

evidence.soft_delete: OrderItem.php:8 + use SoftDeletes on :13 — orders/items soft-deleted preserve composition_snapshot in deleted_at-marked rows
evidence.branch_scope: OrderItem.php:15-28 — `static::addGlobalScope(new BranchScope())` post-iter12 P0-FIX-2 prevents cross-tenant composition_snapshot leak via ItemService::destroy count query

findings.consequence: NF525 6-year retention is preserved by soft-delete pattern + branch scope ensures fiscal data stays within the issuing branch boundary.
